❌ Error: Unknown parameter(s) detected:
  --latency-test
  -x

Note: --latency-test has been renamed to --ram-latency

🚀 Test Memory R (TMR) v1.0.0 - High-Performance Memory Testing Tool
===================================================================================

USAGE:
  tmr.exe                                    # Run with defaults
  tmr.exe config=test.json                  # Load modern JSON config (v2.0)
  tmr.exe config=legacy.cfg                 # Load legacy TestMem5 config (v1.0)
  tmr.exe --create-demo-configs              # Create demo configuration files
  tmr.exe --compare-results baseline.json current.json [output.json]
                                          # Compare two test results from .\results\
  tmr.exe --setup-large-pages              # Configure large pages for optimal performance
  tmr.exe --calibrate-cache                # Measure the cache tiers' sizes; saved to tmr-cfg.json after a prompt
  tmr.exe --calibrate-cache-ext            #   ...finer, around each tier's edge (preferred when both are saved)
  tmr.exe --calibrate-seal                 # Time the seal's fill and check at each width, one thread; seal-width=auto
                                          #   then runs the fastest (a narrower one if it is as fast)
  tmr.exe --calibrate-all                  # --calibrate-cache, then --calibrate-seal (maxpage= sets both's page size)
  tmr.exe plan=stability                   # The default: the stability tests at the widest width (or width=)
  tmr.exe plan=quick                       # The stability tests once
  tmr.exe plan=widths                      # Every width of the tests that have them, side by side
  tmr.exe plan=perf                        # Latency and bandwidth
  tmr.exe plan=all                         # Every test in the suite; test= alone picks from it
  tmr.exe --quick-test                     # plan=quick, reserving 60% of available memory
  tmr.exe --ram-latency                    # Run DRAM latency tests (6 tests)
  tmr.exe --cache-latency                  # Run full cache hierarchy latency tests (12 tests)
  tmr.exe test=Spd-*                       # Run tests matching pattern (glob wildcards)
  tmr.exe test=Mem-Mirror*,Lat-L3-*        # Run multiple patterns (comma-separated)
  tmr.exe config=x.cfg --startup-debug     # Print the memory and test plan; allocate no test memory, run nothing
  tmr.exe --version                         # Show version information
  tmr.exe --show-topology                   # Show CPU Topology Mapping for debugging
  tmr.exe --debug-topology                  # Runs multiple CPU Topology checks to debug if one works better

EXIT STATUS: 0 passed, 1 tests failed or found errors, 2 stopped before or instead of testing
             (bad config, failed command), 3 interrupted (Ctrl+C); other codes: crashed or killed
             (errors=panic aborts on the first error)

COMMAND LINE PARAMETERS:
  memory=20%                           # Reserve 20% of system memory
  memory=2GiB                         # Reserve 2 GiB
  memory=2048MB                       # TM5-compatible allocation (2048MB from available)
  memory=10%-from-available           # Reserve 10% from currently available memory
  memory=8GiB-from-total              # Reserve 8 GiB from total system memory
  memory=64GiB-target                 # Target 64 GiB allocation (may fail if unavailable)
  cycles=5                            # Run 5 complete test cycles
  duration=600                        # Maximum 10 minutes runtime
  cpus=50%                            # Use 50% of available CPUs
  cputype=cores                       # Use physical cores (vs threads/SMT)
  skip-cores=1                        # Stage 1 FILTER: skip first N CPUs (default: 1 to preserve OS)
  skip-cores=25%                      #   ...or skip the leading N% (portable across core counts)
  skip-cores=0-7                      #   ...or exclude a core-id range (isolate a memory domain/CCD)
  cpu-stride=2                        # Stage 2 SPACING: use every Nth available CPU
  cpu-stride=even                     #   ...or spread the requested count evenly across the pool
  --disable-pinning                   # Disable CPU thread pinning
  priority=high                       # Worker priority: normal, high (default), realtime
                                      #   realtime is THREAD_PRIORITY_TIME_CRITICAL, the top of the
                                      #   normal range (not the realtime class); leave a core free with it
  hugechunk=1GiB                      # First 1GB-page request size, halved on refusal (power of two, >= 1GiB)
  largechunk=128MiB                   # First 2MB-page request size, halved on refusal (default 128MiB)
  largefloor=16MiB                    # Smallest 2MB-page request (16MiB-1GiB)
  blkroundtarget=1GiB                 # Round each thread's share to a multiple of this (of largefloor)
  blkround=up                         # ...up (default; a smaller step rather than pass available), down, or nearest
  errors=halt                         # Error handling (log/halt/panic)
  seal=tmr                            # Seal: check and reseal around every chunk (tmr, the default; tm5; off)
  seal-width=auto                     # Seal kernels' SIMD width (auto, 128, 256, 512); unset, width='s;
                                      #   auto is --calibrate-seal's width on this machine, else 256
  width=auto                          # SIMD width of the tests that pick theirs at run time (the -Auto
                                      #   tests, Mem-Sequence, the Bench pairs) and of the seal: auto (the
                                      #   widest the CPU has; the seal its own auto), 128, 256 or 512
                                      #   (refused if the CPU lacks it). Mem-Sequence has no 128 and runs
                                      #   at 256; -128/-256/-512 tests keep theirs
  mirror=whole                        # Mirror tests: one mirror over each chunk (the default)
  mirror=subblocks:4                  #   ...each chunk in 2 or 4 parts, mirrored in lockstep
  mirror=jump:510                     #   ...128 B swaps every (N+1) x 128 B (TM5 MirrorMove128)
  pattern-mode=0                      # Pattern mode: 0-2 (TM5's), 10, 11, 13, 20, 30 (TMR's), or a native
                                      #   family alone on SimpleTest: 15 ident, 16 random, 17 linepair,
                                      #   21 lines, 31 switch, 32 quiet, 33 header; unset, SimpleTest runs
                                      #   native programs (doc/pattern_spec.md)
  sequence=W,2R,RW,2R@random          # Mem-Sequence's passes: W writes, R reads, RW reads and writes each line;
                                      #   a count before, an @order after (spaces or commas between)
  order=random                        # Mem-Sequence's order where a step names none: forward, reverse, random,
                                      #   stride (TM5's, from a config entry's parameter)
  patterns=legacy                     # A TM5 .cfg's SimpleTest modes as TMR's numbered modes, not native
                                      #   programs (default native), to compare the two
  seed=0x1234                         # The native patterns' run seed (default: from the clock, logged and
                                      #   saved in the results), to replay a run's bytes
  beat=32                             # Transfer width the switch pattern flips at: auto (SMBIOS, the
                                      #   default), 16 (LPDDR4/5), 32 (DDR5), 64 (DDR4), or a memory
                                      #   type (ddr4, ddr5, lpddr5, ...); 12 (lpddr6) and 24 (ddr6) are
                                      #   models: TMR hasn't verified their packet maps
  rescan=off                          # A failed check isn't rescanned to name each bad word (default on;
                                      #   off counts one error a failed check, for runs with many errors)
  verify-reps=5                       # Verify passes per write (TM5 retention stress: 5)
  test-reps=3                         # Test op repetitions per write (MirrorMove round-trips)
  write-read-cycles=4                 # Write+verify cycles per chunk (TM5 SimpleTest: 4)
  topology=windowsv2                  # Core types from one detector alone (default auto, the cascade):
                                      #   windows efficiency class, windowsv2 Windows' core priority,
                                      #   cpuid L3 size per core, amd AMD's CPUID core type
  core-priority=hybrid                # Hybrid CPUs that report no core types (e.g. Ryzen 8500G):
                                      #   Windows' higher-priority cores are P-cores (default: equal)
  --no-calibration                    # Skip loading calibration data (use CPUID heuristics; the seal's rule)

CONFIG FILE OVERRIDES:
  All parameters can override config file values:
    tmr.exe config=test.json cycles=1 skip-cores=0 memory=4GiB

LOGGING:
  RUST_LOG=info                       # Set log level (error/warn/info/debug/trace)
                                        # Use debug for detailed per-thread logs
  Logs saved to: .\logs\TMR_YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS.log      (local time)
  Results saved to: .\results\TMR_YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS.json (same name as the log)

RESULT COMPARISON:
  Test results are automatically saved as JSON files to .\results\
  Use --compare-results to analyze performance differences
  Useful for memory overclocking and timing optimization

Quick Usage Examples:
  tmr.exe memory=10%-from-available     # Standard: Reserve 10% from currently available memory
  tmr.exe memory=2048MB                 # TM5 compatible: Reserve 2048MB from available memory
  tmr.exe memory=8GiB-from-total        # Failure test: Reserve 8 GiB from total (unrealistic)
  tmr.exe memory=64GiB-target           # Failure test: Target 64 GiB allocation (may fail)
  tmr.exe cycles=5 duration=600        # 5 cycles OR 10 minutes max
  tmr.exe cpus=50% cputype=cores       # Use 50% of CPU cores (cores=avoid SMT)
  tmr.exe skip-cores=0                 # Don't skip any CPUs (default: skip first CPU)
  tmr.exe skip-cores=0-7 cpus=100%     # Test ONLY cores 8+ (isolate a memory domain on multi-CCD parts)
  tmr.exe cpus=50% cpu-stride=even     # Spread half the cores evenly (loads all memory domains equally)
  tmr.exe --disable-pinning            # Disable CPU pinning (default: enabled)
  tmr.exe errors=halt                  # Stop on first error
  tmr.exe config=test.json             # Load comprehensive JSON config
  tmr.exe config=legacy.cfg            # Auto-convert TM5 config + add stuck bit test
  tmr.exe --create-demo-configs        # Create demo configurations
  tmr.exe --compare-results old.json new.json # Compare results from .\results\
